Get and resolve cell edits in Shiny

Source: R/editing.R
reactable-editing.Rd

getReactableEdit() reactively returns the latest submitted cell edit. Use it in shiny::observeEvent() and call resolveReactableEdit() after validating and saving the value. The application must validate row IDs, editable columns, permissions, types, and business rules on the server. Columns with editValidation = FALSE apply submissions locally without waiting for a response. They still notify Shiny, but do not display a server-validation success indicator, and ignore resolutions. This mode does not provide server validation or persistence.

Usage

getReactableEdit(outputId, session = NULL)

resolveReactableEdit(
  outputId,
  edit,
  value = edit$value,
  error = NULL,
  session = NULL
)

Arguments

outputId

The Shiny output ID of the reactable instance.

session

The Shiny session. Defaults to the current reactive domain.

edit

An edit returned by getReactableEdit().

value

The accepted value, optionally normalized by the server. Defaults to the submitted value. Use NULL for a missing numeric or date value.

error

A nonempty error message to reject the edit, or NULL to accept it.

Value

getReactableEdit() returns NULL before the first edit, or a list containing editId, inputId, rowId, columnId, oldValue, and value. Row IDs and column IDs are strings; dates in this list are ISO date strings. resolveReactableEdit() returns invisibly.

Details

Native input values are also available individually as input[[id]]. Text and number inputs submit on blur or Enter; textareas submit on blur or Ctrl/Cmd+Enter. Select and checkbox inputs submit immediately. Dates submit on blur, Enter, or a calendar selection. Escape restores the confirmed value.
